comments.text_zh: 因《The Continuity of Splines》[0] 而闻名的 Freya Holmer 最近做了一场很棒的会议演讲，讲的是：只要你接受一条新公理：v^2 = ||v||^2，也就是“向量的平方等于其模长的平方”，那么四元数就会自然地产生于定义两个向量乘法的愿望之中。内容既迷人又有趣，我强烈推荐任何觉得这东西有意思但又感到困惑（像我一样）的人去看看：[LINK] [0] [VIDEO]
comments.text: Freya Holmer, of The Continuity of Splines [0] fame, recently gave a great conference talk about how quaternions naturally arise from the desire to define the multiplication of two vectors if you just agree to one new axiom : v^2 = ||v||^2, or "the square of a vector is equal to the square of its norm". It was fascinating and entertaining and I highly recommend anyone who finds this stuff interesting but confusing (like I do) to check it out: [LINK] [0] [VIDEO]

comments.why_zh: 举例说明你可能需要的特定算法视频。
comments.text_zh: 我一直在重新学习 CS（小时候编过程，退伍后上大学时，差一门 300 级课程就能拿到 CS 辅修——而那门课在我需要的时候没有重新开课），后来日常工作就只用 (La)TeX 和 AppleScript，但现在正试着为 CNC 做一个工具，它和以前已有的那些工具相当不同；有一件事帮了很大忙，就是 MIT OCW：- Python 课程让我快速掌握了这门语言的基础：[LINK] 和 [LINK] - 《Structure and Interpretation of Computer Programs》则像是一次有纪律的复习，帮我重新过了一遍这本我初读时没耐心做习题的书：[LINK] - 《Mathematics for Computer Science》帮我补上了我零零散散的数学基础：[LINK] 我还发现最近这本书 [LINK] 非常有用（第一次读时，我一次读一章，并按照那一章的原则重写我当前的项目）——这里有一个有趣的视频概览：[LINK] 如果运气好，还能找到针对自己需要的特定主题/算法的视频，例如：[VIDEO]
comments.text: I've been re-learning CS (programmed as a kid, then missed getting a minor in CS in college after the service by one 300-level course which wasn't being re-offered when I needed it) and then just did (La)TeX and AppleScript for my day job, but am now trying to create a tool for CNC which is quite different from those which have existed previously, and one thing which has helped a lot is MIT OCW: - the Python courses got me up-to-speed on the basics of that language: [LINK] and [LINK] - Structure and Interpretation of Computer Programs served as a disciplined review of a book which I wasn't patient enough to do the exercises of when I first read it: [LINK] - Mathematics for Computer Science helped make up for my spotty math: [LINK] I've also found the recent book: [LINK] very helpful (first reading I did one chapter at a time, re-writing my current project applying the principles of that chapter) --- interesting video overview at: [LINK] If one is fortunate, there are videos on specific subjects/algorithms which one needs, e.g., [VIDEO]
